svg.title: Before: me as the router between every agent thread
svg.desc: A dark terminal-style diagram. A blocky figure labelled Me sits at the top left. Beside it, the chores I have to do for every thread: start it on the right machine, notice when a turn finishes, read what it did, answer its questions, decide what to do next. Below, twelve attention cells, one per thread: the first is fine, up to five are OK, and the rest are amber warnings labelled beyond that, things break down. At the bottom are three machines, two macOS and one Linux, each running T3 Code with four agent threads for the news reader, game and research desk projects on Codex or Claude. A cable drops from me and splits into a tangle of wires, one to every thread. Most threads are amber and waiting on me: turn finished, has a question, what's next. One dashed thread is an iOS task sitting on the Linux machine, the wrong machine.
svg.text: start it on the right machine
MY ATTENTION, ONE CELL PER THREAD
